name: Amphitheatre
period: late 3rd century AD (c. 270–280): the stone phase (arena wall, entrance passages and recesses rebuilt in stone in the first half of the 3rd century; arena, recess and passage floors raised with sand and gravel, Fulford's Stone Phase 2, c. 250s)

frame.note: local u (east-ish), v (north-ish) metres from the SW corner of the key anchor; E,N = origin + R(angle)*(u,v). Arena wall, passages and recesses from GIS layer 04 (stone phase); banks from the Fulford 2002 contour plan.

conventions: arena: wall centreline as polar samples [deg ccw from +u, radius] about c; heights in metres above the arena floor; d = metres outward from the wall centreline along the ray from c. conjecture:true marks things not evidenced.

drawings.caption: Section along the arena through both entrances, looking west: the passages rise from the arena to the old ground level; the west seating beyond
Section across the arena through the two recesses, looking north: arena wall, timber rows on the earth banks, the walk and fence at the top, the outer slope

arena.note: Stone arena wall of flint and brown ironstone, about 3 m high (Fulford 2002); 0.8-0.9 m thick (Fulford 1989, 37). Plan from the GIS (stone phase). The arena floor lies about 2 m below the original ground (C&F 2016; Fulford 2002).

rail.note: Timber rail on the arena wall, as on Fulford's reconstruction section (Fulford 2002). Conjecture.

seating.note: Timber seating on the earth bank: 12 rows as on Fulford's reconstruction of the stone phase (Fulford 2002); Sunter (in Fulford 1989) reconstructs 11 or 12 rows raised on radial timbers. Row size from the section.

bank.note: Earth banks built from the soil dug out of the arena (C&F 2016; Fulford 2002); extent from the surviving earthwork (Fulford 2002 contour plan). Crest height from the reconstruction section.

palisade.note: Fence along the back of the seating: a post on Fulford's section; a free-standing palisade closed the top of the cavea in the first timber phase (Sunter in Fulford 1989, via Kovacsovics 1993).

passages.note: North entrance: open passage walled in stone (GIS stone phase), clear width about 5.3 m; it rises from the arena to the old ground level. Its collapse is recorded later (Fulford 1989, via Kovacsovics 1993).
South entrance: open passage walled in stone, clear width about 3.8 m against the north entrance's 5.3 m (GIS stone phase): the entrances differ in width (Fulford 1989, via Kovacsovics 1993).

recesses.note: West recess: a small semicircular room opening off the arena (GIS stone phase), probably vaulted (Fulford 2002). Its use is unknown: altars to Nemesis stood in similar recesses elsewhere; or a refuge for participants (Fulford 2002).

East recess: a small semicircular room opening off the arena (GIS stone phase), probably vaulted (Fulford 2002). Its use is unknown: altars to Nemesis stood in similar recesses elsewhere; or a refuge for participants (Fulford 2002).

stairs.note: Stair up the outside of the bank to the seats: conjecture. The first timber phase was reached by stairs from outside (Sunter in Fulford 1989, via Kovacsovics 1993); positions are not known.
